decisions.title: How should personal-jacky project notes be seeded?
decisions.context: Claude Desktop MCP works; portfolio notes (ViOS, melody-thesis, …) are still thin. Autopilot should not invent personal content.

options.label: Founder + Claude Desktop seed manually (recommended)
options.implication: E-05 stays proposed; no Maker tasks until you ask.

options.label: Approve a Maker task that only creates stub notes with titles + links from project-registry.md
options.implication: Low-risk stubs; you fill bodies later.

decisions.recommendation: A — content quality matters more than stubs for a personal knowledge hub.
decisions.decided_note: Founder 2026-08-07: seed via Claude Desktop / manual; Autopilot must not invent personal note bodies.

decisions.title: Which credentials does the hub get, and scoped how?
decisions.context: E-09 collectors need two credentials the founder must create by hand. (1) A GitHub token that can READ jackyckma/{orbita,ai-transformation-io,powerhouse,ai-business,ViOS} — three are private, and an unauthenticated read returns 404, which a naive collector would record as 'no activity' rather than 'no access'. (2) A Zeabur API key for https://api.zeabur.com/graphql. NO BUILD WAS REQUIRED: the credential vault already existed and runs in production — packages/lane-credentials, mounted at POST /v1/admin/credentials, write-once (409 on duplicate client_id+name), AES-encrypted with ORBITA_SECRETS_KEY, secret never returned by any read route. Agents resolve secrets server-side via resolveCredentialSecret(clientId, name), already wired into the agent turn runner.

options.label: Fine-grained GitHub PAT (contents: read-only, those 5 repos) + Zeabur API key (recommended)
options.implication: Least privilege available on both platforms. The Zeabur key is still account-wide — a platform limit, not a choice — so treat it as sensitive and rotate if the hub is ever exposed.

options.label: GitHub token only; defer Zeabur
options.implication: Line 1 works for all five projects; the merged-but-never-deployed blind spot stays open. T-0052 blocks.

options.label: Use a GitHub App instead of a PAT
options.implication: Better rotation and per-repo scoping, but meaningfully more setup for a single-operator portfolio.

decisions.recommendation: A — B leaves open the specific failure that is hardest to notice by eye (build fails, task still says done, prod smoke passes on the previous deployment). C is the right answer at larger scale, not at five repos with one operator.
decisions.decided_note: Founder 2026-08-09: both credentials created and stored under client_id personal-jacky, and verified present via GET /v1/admin/credentials — github_read (scopes: repo:read) and zeabur_api (scopes: deploy:read), both created 2026-08-09T18:45Z. GitHub token is a fine-grained PAT limited to the five registered repos with Contents=Read-only. T-0051 and T-0052 are unblocked and can now be verified against real data rather than fixtures. NOTE FOR THE IMPLEMENTER: resolve secrets by name via resolveCredentialSecret(db, secretsKey, 'personal-jacky', 'github_read' | 'zeabur_api'). Never read them into a log, a report body, an error message, or a committed file. A 404 from a registered private repo means the token lost access — surface it as a collector FAILURE, never as an empty report.

_procedure._doc: CANONICAL credential names live here, not duplicated into task descriptions — T-0051/T-0052 unblock from this decision, so they inherit these. If a name changes, change it here only.
_procedure.write_once: Duplicate client_id+name returns 409 on POST. rotation: use PUT /v1/admin/credentials/{client_id}/{name} with a new secret (no SQL needed); DELETE with ?confirm=<name> to remove. NOTE: a fine-grained PAT's permissions can be edited on GitHub without regenerating the token, so widening or narrowing access does NOT require touching the vault row.

credentials.name: github_read
credentials.source: GitHub > Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens > Fine-grained. Repository access: only jackyckma/{orbita,ai-transformation-io,powerhouse,ai-business,ViOS}. Permission: Contents = Read-only. Nothing else.

_procedure.verify: GET https://api.get-orbita.com/v1/admin/credentials with the same admin header — returns metadata only. Secrets are never returned; seeing the two names listed is the confirmation.

_why_read_only._doc: Founder asked 2026-08-09 whether to grant Contents:write now, since instruction dispatch into each repo is coming (E-07 H3). Decision: NO. Recorded so a future session does not widen this token by reflex.
reasons: DIFFERENT TRIGGER, DIFFERENT RISK. github_read is used by an UNATTENDED job on a schedule. Every repo it touches auto-deploys to production on merge to main. An unattended scheduled process holding write to five production repos is the single worst place to put that permission. Dispatch, by contrast, only ever runs after a founder gate.
NOTHING WRITES YET. Every task in E-09 (T-0050..T-0053) is read-only by design. E-07 H3 (dispatch) is not even an approved epic — it has not been decomposed.

THE GATE IS AT THE CONVERSATION LAYER BY DESIGN (portfolio-hub.md). Writes are supposed to happen with a human present. That path already works today: Claude writes each repo's backlog during a session with the founder. Automating it is an optimization, not a missing capability — and a scheduled unattended writer would move the gate to the wrong place.

BLAST RADIUS. Read-only means a buggy or looping collector produces a wrong report. Write means wrong commits on main of five auto-deploying repos. The first is a bad afternoon; the second is a bad week.

UPGRADING IS CHEAP. A fine-grained PAT's permissions can be edited without regenerating the token, so the stored secret stays valid and the write-once vault row does NOT need replacing. There is no lock-in penalty for starting narrow.
_why_read_only.when_dispatch_ships: Create a SEPARATE credential named github_dispatch with contents:write (and pull_requests:write if dispatch goes via PR), used only by the gated dispatch path — never by the collectors. Note that fine-grained PATs cannot scope to paths: any write token can modify source code, not just docs/autopilot/*.json. That is a further argument for PR-based dispatch, so the target repo's own Checker reviews what the hub proposes rather than the hub pushing straight to main.

decisions.title: Set the hub tenant explicitly in Zeabur, then remove the hard-coded default
decisions.context: E-14 phase 1 adds explicit tenant config (for example ORBITA_HUB_CLIENT_ID) and keeps the old hard-coded 'personal-jacky' only as a warned fallback so production keeps booting. Phase 2 removes the fallback so an unset tenant fails at startup. Only the founder can set Zeabur environment variables. Tenants will later be separate servers, so a hard-coded identity must not survive.

options.label: Set ORBITA_HUB_CLIENT_ID (and the OAuth default client id) in Zeabur, then approve removal of the fallback
options.implication: production is explicit; if a variable is forgotten the API fails at startup - verify the warning log first

options.label: Keep the warned fallback for now
options.implication: works, but the hard-coded identity stays and every new tenant server must override it

decisions.recommendation: A, after confirming in the Zeabur logs that the deprecated-default warning no longer appears

decisions.title: Create the GitHub App and its credentials for near-real-time git sync
decisions.context: E-15 builds the receiver, App-auth and sync code behind ORBITA_GITHUB_APP_ENABLED (default off). Activating it needs credentials only the founder can create: a GitHub App (repository permission Contents: read-only, event Push, installed on the portfolio registry repositories), then the webhook secret, private key (.pem), App id and installation id stored in the Orbita credential vault through POST /v1/admin/credentials (write-once; never paste them into chat), then the flag set in Zeabur. D-002 option C (GitHub App) was earlier judged heavy; the founder chose it on 2026-10-01 because it also replaces the long-lived read token with short-lived read-only tokens.

options.label: Create the App now and store the credentials
options.implication: activation task can run; webhook points at /v1/inbound/github on api.get-orbita.com

options.label: Postpone
options.implication: sync stays daily; the portfolio brief stays up to a day stale

decisions.recommendation: A once E-15's receiver is deployed with the flag off (the endpoint must exist before the App is pointed at it)

decisions.title: Enable the ticket system in production (ORBITA_TICKETS_ENABLED=1)
decisions.context: E-16 ships tickets behind ORBITA_TICKETS_ENABLED (default off): flag off means no DDL, no routes, no MCP tools, no behaviour change. Switching it on creates the new tables at the next API start (runMigrations has no try/catch and runs before the server listens, so a faulty DDL would stop production from booting).

options.label: Enable after the checklist: e2e-tier-a green with the flag on in GitHub CI, and the DDL applied twice on a scratch database
options.implication: low risk, tickets available to agents

options.label: Keep off
options.implication: nothing changes; E-17 principals have nothing to protect yet

decisions.title: Move agent scope checks from shadow to enforce, and create principals for real agents
decisions.context: E-17 adds per-agent principals and tool-level scopes. Mode shadow only logs would-deny decisions; enforce blocks. Existing keys keep working as the built-in 'legacy-full' principal. Before any external agent (for example a Grok Bot that browses untrusted pages) is connected it needs its own least-privilege principal that cannot call github_*, trigger_automation, admin or note writes.

options.label: Review the shadow audit log for a week, then enforce; create bot principals afterwards
Enforce immediately
options.implication: faster, risk of blocking a legitimate tool call

options.label: Stay in shadow
options.implication: no protection yet; do not connect external agents

decisions.title: Remove the waitlist feature entirely?
decisions.context: The waitlist is a complete feature, not a placeholder: public POST /v1/waitlist (email + optional message, no rate limit or captcha, CORS allow-list), admin approval that ALWAYS creates an API key (scopes sessions:create, sessions:use) and optionally emails it in plain text through Zeabur ZSend, table waitlist_entries, tests, the public page apps/orbita-web/public/waitlist.html (posts to https://api.get-orbita.com/v1/waitlist) linked from the home page and updates page, docs and two prod e2e scripts. It serves a hosted self-signup model; the direction chosen on 2026-10-01 is consulting deployments (one server per tenant), where nobody signs up on a public list. It also adds an unauthenticated public write endpoint and emails a live API key. Removing it changes documented public behaviour of get-orbita.com/waitlist. The admin UI only lists PENDING entries, so existing approved/rejected/pending rows must be checked before anything is dropped.

options.label: Remove it: code, public page and link, docs, scripts, env vars; keep the table untouched until you export or drop it
options.implication: smaller surface and no public write endpoint; the website page must be replaced by a contact link; do the pre-removal checklist first

options.label: Keep as is
options.implication: nothing changes; keep the unprotected public endpoint and the plaintext-key email

options.label: Keep but harden (rate limit/captcha, never email keys)
options.implication: still maintained for a model you are not pursuing

decisions.recommendation: A, after the checklist: (1) list ALL waitlist rows (any status) - via the API/DB, not only the pending view; (2) export real signups if any and decide whether those people need a reply; (3) decide what get-orbita.com shows instead of the waitlist page; (4) then approve removal.
decisions.decided_note: 2026-10-02 founder (hub session) approved A: remove the waitlist entirely, including the public page on get-orbita.com WITHOUT a replacement for now. Verified before deciding: waitlist_entries had 5 rows, all status approved, emails on example.com/gmail.com dated 2026-06-24..26 = e2e/dev tests, no real signups; the five waitlist-* API keys (and nine smoke keys) were revoked by the founder on 2026-10-02. The table waitlist_entries stays in production untouched until the founder drops it AFTER the code removal is deployed, because every boot runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for it.
